title: A Single Suffix to Break Them All: Basin-Aware Jailbreaks for Merged Model Families
abstract: arXiv:2608.26506v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Model merging enables combining multiple fine-tuned models without additional training, but its safety implications remain poorly understood. Prior work primarily attributes merging risks to unsafe constituent models, implicitly assuming that merging individually aligned models preserves safety. In contrast, we show that model merging reveals a previously overlooked jailbreak risk rooted in the pretrained foundation model, even when all constituent models are individually safety-aligned. Motivated by this observation, we study a new threat setting where an attacker constructs jailbreak prompts that generalize across merged models sharing the same pretrained backbone, without access to the exact merging coefficients or constituent checkpoints. translated_title: 一个后缀破解所有：针对合并模型族的盆地感知越狱攻击
translated_abstract: 模型合并技术能够在不进行额外训练的情况下组合多个微调模型，但其安全性影响仍未被充分理解。以往研究主要将合并风险归因于不安全的组成模型，并隐含假设合并各自对齐的模型能保持安全性。相反，我们表明模型合并揭示了一种先前被忽视的越狱风险，该风险根源于预训练基础模型，即使所有组成模型都经过单独的安全对齐。基于这一观察，我们研究了一种新的威胁场景，其中攻击者构造的越狱提示能够泛化到共享同一预训练骨干的合并模型上，而无需访问确切的合并系数或组成检查点。为利用这一现象，我们提出了**盆地感知越狱（BAJ）**，它将越狱生成表述为合并空间上的最小-最大优化，以产生可迁移的对抗性后缀。
tldr: 我们发现了模型合并中源于预训练基础模型的隐蔽越狱风险，并提出盆地感知越狱（BAJ）方法，通过最小-最大优化生成跨合并模型族可迁移的对抗后缀。
en_tdlr: We uncover a hidden jailbreak risk rooted in the pretrained foundation model during model merging, and propose Basin-Aware Jailbreak (BAJ) to generate transferable adversarial suffixes via min-max optimization across merged model families.
